_comment: The v3.0.0 active machine-readable artifact contract, applied to the LIVE registry/artifact-capabilities-registry.json and the LIVE `git ls-files` set. Until governance/check/active-artifact-contract/tests/active_artifact_contract_live.rs landed, this doctrine had never produced a verdict about this codebase: the crate's only Cargo consumer was marketplace/facade/dev-cli, which no workflow invokes, so every case the kernel had ever run was a hand-written fixture inside src/lib.rs — while two registry rows had been pointing `artifact_path` at directories that are not tracked files. Every set below is pinned by EQUALITY over the UNION of the frozen and observed keys, so every one is TWO-SIDED: a new observation blocks, and a frozen observation that stops being produced ALSO blocks until it is struck in the same change. The min_* floors count SUBJECT rows and tracked paths, never findings, so no floor here can red on honest progress.
authority: ADR-0709 (live apex), which restates the ADR-0069 v3.0.0 contract
_authority_note: ADR-0069 is Superseded, superseded_by ADR-0709, and its archived file is stamped HISTORICAL / NON-AUTHORITY. It is cited here only as provenance. The live restatement was checked rather than assumed: ADR-0709 carries the ADR-0069 clause twice — in its consolidated decision list and again in its residual section — naming the v3.0.0 contract, its format-agnostic scope, and its registry-pattern control plane (control plane in the registry, data plane in the artifacts). The doctrine is therefore live law and a connect candidate, not a delete candidate.
subject: every row of registry/artifact-capabilities-registry.json, `_self_row` included, checked against the HEAD-tracked path set from `git ls-files`
_scope_is_R01_R02_and_that_limit_is_itse: The kernel implements seven rules. Only R01 (artifact_path is HEAD-tracked) and R02 (no duplicate artifact_id) have any input in this corpus: R03-R07 are all functions of a per-capability `status`, and NO ROW ANYWHERE DECLARES ONE. The registry uses the profile system instead — `artifact_profile` plus a sparse `capability_overrides` block that carries lane ids, crate paths and metric definitions but never a status. A caller that resolved the missing statuses from the kernel's profile defaults would report 765 R05 violations that describe the caller's own defaulting choice and nothing about the registry, which is manufacturing findings, not enforcing a doctrine. So this gate binds R01 and R02, and `frozen_rows_declaring_capability_status` makes the omission SELF-RETIRING rather than silent: it is an equality-pinned EMPTY set, so the first row to declare a real status reddens this gate and forces the caller to be widened into R04-R07 in that change. A scope limit that cannot notice when it stops applying is an excuse; this one is a tripwire.
_measured_2026_08_19: Measured on dev @ 889027711 (the commit that deleted 51 unreferenced product crates): 13746 tracked paths; 85 registry rows (84 in `rows` plus `_self_row`), all with distinct artifact_ids. 2 rows declare an artifact_path that is not HEAD-tracked, and both are the same defect — the value names a DIRECTORY that exists on disk (registry/check-empirical-evidence/, registry/loop-recovery-patterns/) while the contract's rule is a tracked-PATH rule, so `git ls-files` never yields it. 4 rows declare an artifact_profile outside the kernel's closed 7-value enum. 0 rows declare any per-capability status.
_frozen_untracked_artifact_paths_note: Keyed `<artifact_id>::<artifact_path>`, the id and the exact declared value, so the entry is reviewable without opening the registry. Both are directories, so both are repairable in one of two honest ways: point the row at the tracked file inside the directory that actually carries the artifact, or split the row per file. Either repair must strike its line here in the same change. The leading slash is preserved verbatim — the caller strips it before the tracked-path lookup (the registry writes repo-absolute paths, `git ls-files` emits repo-relative ones), but the frozen key shows what the registry SAYS, so a reviewer can see the declaration rather than the caller's normalization.
_frozen_duplicate_artifact_ids_note: R02. Empty TODAY and empty is the correct pin: all 85 ids are distinct. Equality-pinned, so the first collision blocks rather than joining a tolerated backlog — a duplicated artifact_id silently makes one of the two rows unreachable to every consumer that keys on the id. This is an equality pin, NOT a floor: a floor on a zero-target term would red on honest progress.
_frozen_unknown_artifact_profiles_note: Keyed `<artifact_id>::<artifact_profile>`. `ArtifactProfile::parse` is a CLOSED enum of seven profiles and these four rows name values outside it, so `specs/artifact-profile-defaults.json` supplies them no defaults and any profile-driven resolution silently treats them as undefined. Frozen as a set rather than a count so each divergence is attributable, and two-sided so neither a fifth unknown profile nor a quietly-repaired one passes unrecorded. Repair is either widening the kernel's enum or moving the row onto an existing profile; both are reviewable edits and both must strike the entry here.
_frozen_rows_declaring_capability_status: The tripwire described in `_scope_is_R01_R02_and_that_limit_is_itself_machine_checked`. Keyed `<artifact_id>::<capability>` for any row whose `capability_overrides` carries a `status` field. Empty today. When it stops being empty this gate reddens, and the correct response is NOT to add the row here — it is to teach the caller to feed real statuses to the kernel so R04-R07 start running.
